look_here_first: LOOK FIRST underground: tough/wiry stolons and usually small (~3–8 mm) tubers distinguish purple nutsedge in combination with persistent, often purplish/red-brown ~2.6–3.4 mm scales. Don't rely on reddish seedhead color by itself.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Introduced perennial sedge, frequently colonial in cultivated or disturbed ground.

key_traits.label: Underground
key_traits.text: Hard, wiry stolons bearing tubers commonly 3–8 mm; compare with yellow nutsedge softer stolons and usually larger tubers.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Terminal umbel-like rays with flattened spikelets; scales often red-purple-brown but variable.

key_traits.label: Scales
key_traits.text: Persistent mature floral scales often ~2.6–3.4 mm with reddish/purple tint; ranges overlap other taxa.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: One-seeded achene; macro of scale and fruit needed for strong ID.
